title: Open the Case File
prompt: Select game_id and game_date from games.
hint: Start with the games table and choose only the two requested columns.
structureHint: Select columns from one table; do not filter or aggregate yet.
solution: SELECT game_id, game_date FROM games ORDER BY game_date;

title: Know the Players
prompt: Return player_id, first_name, and last_name from players.
hint: Use players and select the requested identity columns.
structureHint: Choose columns explicitly and add a deterministic sort.
solution: SELECT player_id, first_name, last_name FROM players ORDER BY last_name, first_name;

title: The Teams on the Board
prompt: Inspect team_id, team_abbreviation, and team_name.
hint: The teams table already contains the readable labels.
structureHint: Select the three team columns; no join is needed.
solution: SELECT team_id, team_abbreviation, team_name FROM teams ORDER BY team_id;

title: Find the First Night
prompt: Find Finals Game 1 using its actual identifier.
hint: Filter games by the identifier ending in 01.
structureHint: Use SELECT, FROM, then WHERE with one equality condition.
solution: SELECT game_id, game_date FROM games WHERE game_id = '0041500401';

title: Cleveland's Roster
prompt: Return Cavaliers player-game records using team_id 1610612739.
hint: The Cavaliers team id is 1610612739.
structureHint: Filter rows with one WHERE condition before ordering.
solution: SELECT player_id, game_id, points FROM player_game_stats WHERE team_id = '1610612739' ORDER BY game_id, player_id;

title: A Closer Look at One Player
prompt: Return one specified player and game record for Game 1.
hint: Combine the game and player filters with AND.
structureHint: Each condition narrows the same row set.
solution: SELECT player_id, game_id, points, assists FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id = '0041500401' AND player_id = '2544';

title: Set the Timeline
prompt: Return all Finals games in chronological order.
hint: Filter the Finals prefix, then sort by game_date.
structureHint: ORDER BY controls result order; never rely on storage order.
solution: SELECT game_id, game_date FROM games WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY game_date ASC;

title: The Scouting Shortlist
prompt: Return the top 10 player-game rows by points with deterministic tie sorting.
hint: Sort points descending and add stable tie-breakers.
structureHint: LIMIT comes after ORDER BY.
solution: SELECT game_id, player_id, points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY CAST(points AS INTEGER) DESC, game_id, player_id LIMIT 10;

title: Count the Evidence
prompt: Count the available Finals games.
hint: COUNT rows from games after filtering the Finals.
structureHint: COUNT(*) returns one aggregate row.
solution: SELECT COUNT(*) AS game_count FROM games WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%';

title: Add Up the Points
prompt: Calculate one player’s points in Game 1.
hint: Filter to one player and one game, then SUM points.
structureHint: Aggregate after applying both filters.
solution: SELECT SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS total_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id = '0041500401' AND player_id = '2544';

title: The Scoreboard Takes Shape
prompt: Calculate both team scores for Game 1.
hint: Group Game 1 rows by team_id.
structureHint: GROUP BY creates one row per team.
solution: SELECT team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS team_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id = '0041500401' GROUP BY team_id ORDER BY team_id;

title: Seven Nights, Seven Margins
prompt: Calculate team scores and Cleveland-minus-Golden-State margin for each game.
hint: Aggregate team scores first, then subtract.
structureHint: The sign convention is Cleveland minus Golden State.
solution: SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, golden_state_points, cleveland_points - golden_state_points AS margin FROM (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id) ORDER BY game_id;

title: Close Games and Blowouts
prompt: Label each game close under a 10-point margin, otherwise decisive.
hint: Use CASE on the derived absolute margin.
structureHint: The boundary is exact: 0–9 close, 10+ decisive.
solution: SELECT game_id, ABS(cleveland_points - golden_state_points) AS margin, CASE WHEN ABS(cleveland_points - golden_state_points) < 10 THEN 'close' ELSE 'decisive' END AS finish_type FROM (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id) ORDER BY game_id;

title: When Is a Group Worth Keeping?
prompt: Return games whose combined team score exceeded 190.
hint: HAVING filters after GROUP BY.
structureHint: This genuinely filters an aggregate.
solution: SELECT game_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS total_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id HAVING SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) > 190 ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Stars' Scoring Averages
prompt: Compare players by total points, games played, and points per game.
hint: Count distinct games and divide safely with NULLIF.
structureHint: HAVING applies the appearance rule after aggregation.
solution: SELECT player_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS total_points, COUNT(DISTINCT game_id) AS games_played, ROUND(SUM(CAST(points AS DOUBLE)) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT game_id), 0), 2) AS points_per_game FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY player_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT game_id) >= 4 ORDER BY total_points DESC;

title: Balanced Team or Star-Led Surge?
prompt: Compare Cleveland scoring in Games 5 and 6.
hint: Use CASE inside SUM, MAX, and COUNT.
structureHint: Keep one row per game and define the threshold.
solution: SELECT game_id, SUM(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN CAST(points AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN CAST(points AS INTEGER) ELSE NULL END) AS top_player_points, COUNT(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' AND CAST(points AS INTEGER) >= 15 THEN 1 END) AS players_15_plus FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id IN ('0041500405', '0041500406') GROUP BY game_id ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Performance Brief
prompt: Produce one row per game with scores, margin, and winner.
hint: Reuse the team-score CTE and add CASE.
structureHint: The grain is exactly one row per game.
solution: SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, golden_state_points, cleveland_points - golden_state_points AS margin, CASE WHEN cleveland_points > golden_state_points THEN 'Cleveland Cavaliers' ELSE 'Golden State Warriors' END AS winner FROM (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id) ORDER BY game_id;

title: Put Names to the Numbers
prompt: Attach player names to player-game statistics.
hint: Join on player_id.
structureHint: Keep the player-game grain.
solution: SELECT s.game_id, s.player_id, p.first_name, p.last_name, s.points FROM player_game_stats s INNER JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.player_id WHERE s.game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY s.game_id, s.player_id;

title: Which Team Was It?
prompt: Attach team abbreviation and name to each player-game row.
hint: Join team_id to teams.
structureHint: Qualify repeated key columns.
solution: SELECT s.game_id, s.player_id, t.team_abbreviation, t.team_name, s.points FROM player_game_stats s INNER JOIN teams t ON t.team_id = s.team_id WHERE s.game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY s.game_id, s.player_id;

title: Place Every Game in Context
prompt: Build a player-by-game report with date, name, team, and points.
hint: Join each foreign key to its matching dimension.
structureHint: The result remains one row per player-game.
solution: SELECT s.game_id, g.game_date, p.first_name, p.last_name, t.team_name, s.points FROM player_game_stats s JOIN games g ON g.game_id = s.game_id JOIN players p ON p.player_id = s.player_id JOIN teams t ON t.team_id = s.team_id WHERE s.game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY s.game_id, s.player_id;

title: Audit the Scoreboard
prompt: Compare game totals after joining games to stats.
hint: Join games on game_id only, then aggregate.
structureHint: Seven rows prove no fan-out.
solution: SELECT s.game_id, SUM(CAST(s.points AS INTEGER)) AS total_points FROM player_game_stats s JOIN games g ON g.game_id = s.game_id WHERE s.game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY s.game_id ORDER BY s.game_id;

title: Build the First CTE
prompt: Rewrite the team-score report using a named intermediate result.
hint: Put the first aggregation inside WITH.
structureHint: The CTE exposes team/game grain.
solution: WITH team_totals AS (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) SELECT game_id, team_id, points FROM team_totals ORDER BY game_id, team_id;

title: The Game 5–6 Comparison
prompt: Compare margins in Games 5 and 6.
hint: Limit the CTE comparison to Games 5 and 6.
structureHint: Statistics show sequence, not causation.
solution: WITH scores AS (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id), games AS (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM scores WHERE game_id IN ('0041500405', '0041500406') GROUP BY game_id) SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, golden_state_points, cleveland_points - golden_state_points AS margin FROM games ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Four-Star Report
prompt: Report series and Game 7 metrics for four named players.
hint: Aggregate series totals separately from Game 7.
structureHint: Keep single-game metrics in distinct aliases.
solution: WITH totals AS (SELECT player_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS series_points, SUM(CAST(assists AS INTEGER)) AS series_assists FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY player_id), game7 AS (SELECT player_id, points AS game7_points, assists AS game7_assists FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id = '0041500407') SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, totals.series_points, totals.series_assists, game7.game7_points, game7.game7_assists FROM totals JOIN game7 ON game7.player_id = totals.player_id JOIN players p ON p.player_id = totals.player_id WHERE (p.first_name, p.last_name) IN (('LeBron','James'),('Kyrie','Irving'),('Stephen','Curry'),('Klay','Thompson')) ORDER BY totals.series_points DESC;

title: The Verified Scorecard
prompt: Build one row per game with scores, margin, and winner.
hint: Use the game-level CTE rather than mixing player rows.
structureHint: Do not duplicate game rows.
solution: SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, golden_state_points, cleveland_points - golden_state_points AS margin, CASE WHEN cleveland_points > golden_state_points THEN 'Cleveland Cavaliers' ELSE 'Golden State Warriors' END AS winner FROM (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id) ORDER BY game_id;

title: Rank the Scorers
prompt: Rank players by total Finals points with ties sharing a rank.
hint: Aggregate player totals before RANK.
structureHint: A grouped player table feeds the window function.
solution: WITH totals AS (SELECT player_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS total_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY player_id) SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, total_points, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_points DESC) AS points_rank FROM totals JOIN players p ON p.player_id = totals.player_id ORDER BY points_rank, p.last_name;

title: Keep Every Box-Score Row
prompt: Show each player-game row with that player’s series total.
hint: Use SUM OVER instead of GROUP BY.
structureHint: Window functions retain original rows.
solution: SELECT game_id, player_id, points, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) OVER (PARTITION BY player_id) AS series_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY player_id, game_id;

title: What Changed Last Night?
prompt: Compare Cleveland points with the previous game.
hint: Create one row per game before LAG.
structureHint: The first change is NULL.
solution: WITH scores AS (SELECT game_id, SUM(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN CAST(points AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS cleveland_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id) SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, cleveland_points - LAG(cleveland_points) OVER (ORDER BY game_id) AS change_from_previous FROM scores ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Momentum Ledger
prompt: Calculate Cleveland cumulative wins chronologically.
hint: Turn each winner into 1 or 0, then use a framed SUM.
structureHint: Order by game_id and state the frame.
solution: WITH winners AS (SELECT game_id, CASE WHEN cleveland_points > golden_state_points THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS cleveland_win FROM (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id)) SELECT game_id, cleveland_win, SUM(cleveland_win) OVER (ORDER BY game_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_cleveland_wins FROM winners ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Scoring Trend
prompt: Calculate Cleveland’s two-game rolling average score.
hint: Aggregate to game grain, then use a two-row frame.
structureHint: The first row uses only available data.
solution: WITH scores AS (SELECT game_id, SUM(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN CAST(points AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS cleveland_points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id) SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, ROUND(AVG(cleveland_points) OVER (ORDER BY game_id ROWS BETWEEN 1 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2) AS rolling_two_game_average FROM scores ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Defensive and Offensive Comparison
prompt: Compare LeBron and Kyrie by game and rank their scoring.
hint: Filter the two players and rank within each game.
structureHint: Partition the rank by game_id.
solution: SELECT game_id, player_id, points, assists, plus_minus, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY game_id ORDER BY CAST(points AS INTEGER) DESC) AS game_scoring_rank FROM player_game_stats WHERE player_id IN ('2544', '202681') AND game_id LIKE '00415004%' ORDER BY game_id, game_scoring_rank;

title: Reconstruct the Series
prompt: Build a report with scores, margin, winner, and running wins.
hint: Build scores, winners, then two running windows.
structureHint: The final row is Cleveland 4, Golden State 3.
solution: WITH games AS (SELECT game_id, cleveland_points, golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id)), winners AS (SELECT *, cleveland_points - golden_state_points AS margin, CASE WHEN cleveland_points > golden_state_points THEN 'Cleveland Cavaliers' ELSE 'Golden State Warriors' END AS winner FROM games) SELECT *, SUM(CASE WHEN winner = 'Cleveland Cavaliers' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (ORDER BY game_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cleveland_wins, SUM(CASE WHEN winner = 'Golden State Warriors' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (ORDER BY game_id ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS golden_state_wins FROM winners ORDER BY game_id;

title: The Final Dossier
prompt: Assemble the seven-row Finals dossier with date, scores, margin, winner, cumulative wins, and final outcome.
hint: Join dates to the verified scorecard and add chronological windows.
structureHint: This is the only challenge exposing the complete final outcome.
solution: WITH scores AS (SELECT game_id, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612739' THEN points END) AS cleveland_points, MAX(CASE WHEN team_id = '1610612744' THEN points END) AS golden_state_points FROM (SELECT game_id, team_id, SUM(CAST(points AS INTEGER)) AS points FROM player_game_stats WHERE game_id LIKE '00415004%' GROUP BY game_id, team_id) scores GROUP BY game_id), winners AS (SELECT g.game_id, g.game_date, s.cleveland_points, s.golden_state_points, s.cleveland_points - s.golden_state_points AS margin, CASE WHEN s.cleveland_points > s.golden_state_points THEN 'Cleveland Cavaliers' ELSE 'Golden State Warriors' END AS winner FROM games g JOIN scores s ON s.game_id = g.game_id) SELECT *, SUM(CASE WHEN winner = 'Cleveland Cavaliers' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (ORDER BY game_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cleveland_wins, 'Cleveland Cavaliers win 4–3' AS final_outcome FROM winners ORDER BY game_date;
